sections.content:
104,420 people

were counted on the census as "financial administrative occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work carry out a variety of finance-related administrative functions not elsewhere classified.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "financial administrative occupations (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "financial administrative occupations (other)", 13.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "financial administrative occupations (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "financial administrative occupations (other)" included:

  • catering and bar managers
  • rail construction and maintenance operatives
  • aerospace engineers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "financial administrative occupations (other)" there were more women than men (71.2% compared with 28.8%).

This means "financial administrative occupations (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 28.8% and women made up 71.2% of "financial administrative occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "financial administrative occupations (other)" included:

  • local government administrative occupations
  • officers of non-governmental organisations
  • waiters and waitresses

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "financial administrative occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "financial administrative occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "financial administrative occupations (other)", 10% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (66.1% compared with 33.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.8%) than self-employed (2.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
